patches.expect: Descend via established rappel routes on the south/east side. Rappel anchors exist on the eastern wall below the summit area. The descent requires technical rope skills and appropriate anchor setup. Alternative descent is to downclimb the South Ridge route if conditions allow.
patches.value: Rappel off the summit by the same line as the peak's other routes: about 35 m north, then a second rappel east onto the Blue Glacier. The last rappel can hang free over the moat at the foot of the face, so land beyond the lip and carry cord to build or back up anchors rather than relying on fixed gear. patches.expect: The most common descent is via rappel anchors on the eastern wall below the summit area. Alternatively, the route can be downclimbed (care needed on the cannon hole feature). patches.value: Do not reverse the ridge. Rappel about 35 m north off the summit, then make a second rappel east onto the Blue Glacier; a moat usually separates rock from ice at the bottom. Carry two 60 m ropes — joined, they give rappels of up to a full 60 m, enough to reach past the lip of the moat — and cord to leave an anchor.

results.fact: Approach distance from Pete Lake Trailhead to Vista Lakes camp
results.evidence: Sources disagree: one route description gives ~5 + 0.6 + 4.5 mi (~10.1 mi) to the Vista Lakes tarns; a backpacking write-up gives 4.5 mi to Pete Lake plus 8.5 mi of PCT switchbacks (~13 mi); another account puts Little Vista Lakes at mile 11.6; a 1986 trip report gives 26 mi round trip including ~2 mi each way to the summit (~11 mi one-way). No two independent sources agree on one figure, so the row's 9 / 10 / 13 mi values are left for a later pass.
